Every nonzero integer has absolute value at least one. Since the product is such an integer and the conjugate has the stated upper bound, the original factor has the lower bound in \eqref{eq:6.7}. The same argument handles \NSi{NS-F-P064-020}{v_t}, using \NSi{NS-F-P064-021}{(n_2-n_1)+\sqrt2\,n_1}. Dividing by either dot product costs at most one power of the frequency size, which is why the inverse directional operators on zero-mean torus functions lose only finitely many torus derivatives. These operators are used in Lemma~\ref{lem:8.2} and in the equations that correct the mean.
